statement: The aggregate `One gate` is the one name to require, and nothing can sit outside it: every job named One gate ... is a need of the aggregate, which reads each need's result, so a new gate job needs no ruleset change; the five names the ruleset requires today (.github/required-checks.json) and the planned `One gate` are each reported by a job of the gate workflow under exactly that name (a matrix job once per value), so renaming a job, or dropping a seed from the matrix, is red in the drift tests instead of leaving a required check that never reports.
source: coordinator 10-01 09:32 (the five One gate checks are required through a ruleset); 10:12 (one aggregate name)

killers.name: R-GATE-CI-CHECK-NAMES a job reports its name, the job id when it has none, and a matrix name once per value
R-GATE-CI-CHECK-NAMES a matrix name with two keys reports every combination, a key used twice is filled everywhere
R-GATE-CI-CHECK-NAMES only the job's own name counts: a name: deeper in the job is not it, and a matrix key with no values reports no name
R-GATE-CI-CHECK-NAMES a workflow with no one-gate job reports nothing, so it is not judged
R-GATE-CI-CHECK-NAMES the required list is read from the contexts of the json, and anything else in it is not a name
R-GATE-CI-CHECK-NAMES the workflow that reports every required name agrees
R-GATE-CI-CHECK-NAMES a renamed job, a seed gone from the matrix, a changed name are each named
R-GATE-CI-CHECK-NAMES a job whose name is dropped reports its id, which is not the required name
R-GATE-CI-CHECK-NAMES an empty required list is a problem of its own, not a pass
R-GATE-CI-CHECK-NAMES a one-gate that needs every One gate (...) job and reads each result agrees
R-GATE-CI-CHECK-NAMES a One gate (...) job that one-gate does not need is named, so adding a job cannot leave it out
R-GATE-CI-CHECK-NAMES a need whose result one-gate never reads is named
R-GATE-CI-CHECK-NAMES a result that is only mentioned, never compared with success, is not tested; an env variable mapped to it is
R-GATE-CI-CHECK-NAMES a gate job, or a step of one, with continue-on-error is named, false is not
R-GATE-CI-CHECK-NAMES every check the ruleset requires is reported by a job of the real workflow
R-GATE-CI-CHECK-NAMES every check planned for the ruleset is reported by a job of the real workflow
R-GATE-CI-CHECK-NAMES the real one-gate needs every One gate (...) job and reads every result
R-GATE-CI-CHECK-NAMES the check is not vacuous: five names are required, and the real One gate workflow reports them
